addendum: Method benchmark, final unseen test, part 2: how the demand of the new months is built, which forecasts are scored, the metrics, the decision rules and the timing. Fixed before any month after August 2026 was downloaded. It scores the forecasts frozen and published under addendum c.
fixed_by: Claude, for Khant Phyo Wai, who asked in chat on 17 Oct 2026 that the work that does not need him be handled in the meantime. The final-test list and the rule that the final test is scored once on months released after the record were agreed with Khant on 15 Oct 2026 (addendum b).
relation: Completes the final unseen test begun in addendum c. For the final test only, it replaces two rules of the record that cannot hold with one to three test months: the eligibility rule (a series enters a comparison with at least 12 test months scored by every pipeline) and the confidence-set inference. Nothing else of the record or of addenda a to c changes.

data_when_fixed.seattle_open_data: No month after 2026-08 has been downloaded or read. The library last refreshed the data on 2026-09-06 and on 2026-10-17 the API listed 2026-01 to 2026-08. The frozen forecasts are in prereg/final_test/forecasts_origin_2026-08.csv, published in the public repository on 2026-10-17 03:24 (merge commit aa7ce72).
data_when_fixed.code: The code for the download, extension, panel and scoring (code/main_study/benchmark/28_final_test_download.py, 29_final_test_world.py, 26_final_test_panel.py, _final_extend.py, 30_final_test_score.py, _final_score.py, and the extended-panel and verification options of 25_final_test_forecast.py) is published in the public repository together with this addendum, and is run exactly as published. A change after this addendum goes to DEVIATIONS.md before it is run. The forecast file itself was checked after those last code changes: the code as published reproduces prereg/final_test/forecasts_origin_2026-08.csv (25_final_test_forecast.py --mode final --origin 2026-08 --verify).

origins_and_target_months: Origin 2026-08 (frozen, addendum c): target months 2026-09, 2026-10 and 2026-11 at horizons 1, 2 and 3. One later origin may be added, 2026-09 (later_origin). The final test can score at most the target months 2026-09 to 2026-12.
release_and_month_checks: A month is released when the API lists rows for it in all three material types. Months are downloaded one at a time, in calendar order, by 28_final_test_download.py (one request a second; the code refuses to run unless this addendum is fingerprinted in prereg/README.md). A download counts only when its row count equals the API's own count for that material type and month, asked again after the download. A month enters the panel only if it passes the Study 3 month rules as coded in study3/_build.month_status: rows present, not fewer than the API's, and a library-wide total not below the closure fraction of the median of the previous months. Rows whose target month fails are not scored; they are listed with the reason.

new_months_in_the_panel.rule: The history is not rebuilt. The stored records, works and theme strengths of the taxonomy v3 build stay as they are and the demand panel of the months to 2026-08 must come out identical (the code stops otherwise). A new row is matched to a stored record by the record key of 10_v3_spl_rows.py. A new record whose work key (_common.assign_work_keys) equals the key of a stored work joins that work and keeps its stored strengths. A record with a work key that no stored work has starts a new work. A new work gets theme strengths by the rules of 16_v3_assign.py from its own records only: OverDrive subject terms of its digital records (source spl) and print subject headings of its print records (source lcsh), through the stored phrase, heading and value-to-node tables; terms and headings the stored tables do not know give no evidence, and there is no Goodreads evidence for a new work. Demand is then sum of checkouts x strength divided by all checkouts of the format and month, as in Study 3, by Study 3's own panel code (26_final_test_panel.py runs study3/01_demand_panel.py's build_seattle on the extended tables).
new_months_in_the_panel.validation_on_known_months: Dry runs on known months before any new month was downloaded (code 27_final_test_dryrun.py; reports data/reports/benchmark_final_test_dryrun.md and benchmark_final_test_dryrun_unseen_vocab.md). The stored rows, records, works and strengths from 2026-06 on were left out; the rows of 2026-06 to 2026-08 (672,478 rows, 25,650 new records, 8,243 new works of which 4,710 got a theme) were brought in again as new rows. The second run also removed the print headings and OverDrive terms that occur only on works first seen from 2026-06 on, so that new works met vocabulary the stored tables do not know, as in the real case. (1) Months before the freeze: the rebuilt panel equals the stored panel (260,944 rows, no difference in any value). (2) Months from the freeze on: for 3,114 series-months the log share of the extended panel minus that of the stored panel (built with the full taxonomy) has a median absolute value of 0.0000 (0.0006 with the unseen vocabulary), a 90th percentile of 0.0007 (0.0064), a 99th percentile of 0.0062 (0.0354) and a largest value of 0.0617 (0.3371), against mean absolute forecast errors of about 0.05. (3) Scoring the stored forecasts of origin 2026-05 (the nine pipelines, horizons 1 to 3) against the extended targets instead of the stored ones changed the pooled error ratio by at most 0.001 (0.004 with the unseen vocabulary), the record's per-series AvgRelMAE by up to 0.026 (0.038), and the mean absolute error by at most 0.01 (0.13) hundredths of log share. (4) The same test with the three months downloaded from the API (28_final_test_download.py --test-months 2026-06,2026-07,2026-08, then 29_final_test_world.py --known-test 2026-06) instead of rebuilt from stored records gave identical counts (25,650 new records, 14,674 of them on stored works, 8,243 new works, 4,710 with a theme) and identical differences (months before the freeze equal to the stored panel, 260,944 rows; median 0.0000, 90th percentile 0.0007, 99th percentile 0.0062, largest 0.0617), so the download, the parsing and the key matching work as tested and the API still returns the stored rows for those months. (5) A harder case, with only one new month: in the world of the freeze month 2026-06 with only the rows of 2026-06 brought in (the evidence of a new work then comes from that month alone: 1,433 of 2,915 new works, 49%, got a theme, against 60% of the 2,823 works first seen in 2026-06 in the stored build, which had two more months of evidence), the extended log shares of 2026-06 were lower than the stored ones by a mean of 0.0074 (median absolute difference 0.0034, 90th percentile 0.020, largest 0.197), and scoring the stored forecasts of origin 2026-05 against them raised the pooled error ratio of each of the eight pipelines by 0.004 to 0.012 (chronos2_cur from 0.911 to 0.916). The new months of the final test are built the same way: the latest released month carries this small downward bias for content that is new, as the last months of the stored panel do, and in this test it worked against the pipelines, so it works against the primary hypothesis.
new_months_in_the_panel.accepted: The rule was accepted as it stood; it was not tuned on these checks.

rows_scored: Rows of the frozen files whose target month passes the month checks and whose share in the extended panel is positive. Series groups: print and ebook (narrow and middle themes), the main group; audiobook, secondary. Rows are (series, origin, horizon).

metrics.pooled_ratio: Sum of the absolute errors of a pipeline in log share divided by the sum of the absolute errors of repeating last month (naive), over the rows where both exist. Below 1 beats repeating last month. This is the primary metric of the final test, because with one to three test months a series has one to three observations and the record's per-series ratio is unstable (on known months it moved by up to 0.04 when the targets changed by a median of at most 0.0006; the pooled ratio moved by at most 0.004, in the dry runs where new works had as much evidence as in the stored build).
metrics.avg_rel_mae: The record's AvgRelMAE (geometric mean over series of MAE of the pipeline / MAE of naive over the series' scored rows), reported beside the pooled ratio; series with a naive error of exactly 0 are left out and counted.
metrics.intervals: 95% intervals from 2,000 resamples of categories (node_id, with all formats, levels, origins and horizons of a node together), seed 20261015: the record's bootstrap, because a month bootstrap has nothing to resample with one to three months.
metrics.rise_task: Spearman correlation across series between the forecast change (forecast - y(t)) and the actual change (y(t+h) - y(t)) within each origin, horizon, format and level group of at least 10 series, averaged over groups; 95% interval from 500 category resamples. Reported, no decision rests on it.
metrics.descriptive: Mean absolute error x 100 and direction accuracy for moves above 0.10, as in the record.

primary_hypothesis: chronos2_cur (Chronos-2 with the concept-page series), the leader of the main comparison A2 (print and ebook, horizon 1, AvgRelMAE 0.914), is more accurate than repeating last month on the new months: at horizon 1, print and ebook, the pooled ratio has a 95% interval whose upper limit is below 1. If so the hypothesis is supported; otherwise it is not supported by these months (with a point estimate below 1 this is reported as "not distinguishable from repeating last month"). The statement needs at least 400 horizon-1 print and ebook rows with an observed target; with fewer the scoring code stops without writing a result and the test waits for the next release (size_and_timing).
secondary_analyses: Every pipeline of the list and the reference against repeating last month: pooled ratio and AvgRelMAE with intervals, at horizons 1, 2 and 3, for print and ebook and for audiobooks.

Paired comparisons with the model held fixed (pooled ratio of the first to the second with interval): chronos2_cur, chronos2_curdw and chronos2_bk each against chronos2; chronos2_curdw against chronos2_cur; catchg_DW and catchg_DWS against catchg_D; chronos2_cur against chronos and against catchg_D. These answer whether the interest inputs helped on the new months; no decision rule.

The rank correlation between the pooled ratios of the pipelines on the new months and in the main comparison (A2 rows, pooled ratio recomputed on the 36,081 rows of that comparison), horizon 1, print and ebook: descriptive.
The rise task (rise_task above) for every pipeline at horizon 1.
not_computed: The model confidence set, the surge average precision and the segments (after short or lasting rises, surge months) need more months or events than the final test has (surges are 0.65% of forecasts, lasting rises 0.4%). The record's horizon-2 and horizon-3 comparisons are reported with the same tables but carry no decision.

size_and_timing.scoring_date: Scored once, by 30_final_test_score.py, on 2026-12-05 or the first later day on which at least one horizon-1 target month is released, passes the month checks and gives at least 400 print and ebook rows. The scoring code refuses to run before 2026-12-05 and with fewer than 400 such rows. All months released and passing the checks on that day are scored; none is left out or waited for.
size_and_timing.once: Numbers computed earlier on known months (the regression, the dry runs and the scoring rehearsal on 2026-06 to 2026-08) are not final-test values. A second scoring run is made only to correct a coding error and is logged in DEVIATIONS.md with the reason; the rules of this addendum do not change after the first run.
size_and_timing.date_change: The date may be moved only by an entry in DEVIATIONS.md made before any new month is scored, for a reason that does not depend on a result (for example the library publishing late).

later_origin: Origin 2026-09 is added if the month 2026-09 is released and downloaded before any 2026-10 row is downloaded. Its forecasts (the same pipelines, horizons 1 to 3, target months 2026-10 to 2026-12) are made by 25_final_test_forecast.py --mode final --origin 2026-09 --panel <extended panel>, frozen in prereg/final_test/ and published to the public repository before any 2026-10 row is downloaded; the interest inputs are those downloaded on 2026-10-13, which end with the week of 2026-09-21. No origin after 2026-09 is added. The effects of lasting rises that began after 2026-06 are not yet in the stored shift-effect table, so catchg_DWS at that origin uses the effects known on 2026-10-13; this is stated in the report. The code was tested for this before the first download, on the dry-run world of the freeze month 2026-06 (data/reports/benchmark_final_test_regression_world.md): at origin 2026-05, whose inputs are identical to the stored ones, all nine pipelines reproduce the stored forecasts (naive and CatBoost exactly, the Chronos models within 1e-6); at origins 2026-06 and 2026-07, whose inputs come from the extension rule, the mean absolute difference from the stored forecasts is at most 0.0046 for CatBoost and 0.0003 for the Chronos models, and the largest single difference is 0.055, in a narrow theme with a very small share. With only one new month (rehearsed with --mode final --rehearsal-dir on the dry-run world that holds 2026-06 alone) the forecasts differ from the stored ones by a mean of 0.006 to 0.010 (largest 0.11), because the new works of the origin month then have less evidence; this is the situation of the origin-2026-09 forecasts, and the stored panel has the same property in its last months.
reporting: The thesis reports the primary hypothesis and the secondary tables as printed by 30_final_test_score.py (data/reports/benchmark_final_test.md), whatever they show. No pipeline, metric or threshold is added or changed after the first scoring run.
disclosures: Seen before fixing: everything listed in addendum c; the frozen forecasts and their summary against naive (mean absolute difference from repeating last month 1.75 to 4.79 hundredths of log share, no target); the dry runs and the scoring rehearsal on the known months 2026-06 to 2026-08, in which chronos2_cur had a pooled ratio of 0.911 at horizon 1 against the stored targets. These months are in the sample of the main comparison.
Not seen: any demand value, theme share or checkout count for a month after 2026-08.
deviations: Changes after this addendum go to prereg/DEVIATIONS.md under "Final unseen test".
